Subject: Greenline AI — SLA/discount ask + proposed mitigation (attachments)

Jonas / Ben,

Following up on our pilot discussions with Greenline AI — procurement just sent over a firm ask: they want a temporary uptimes concession from our standard 99.95% to 99.5% for the first 6 months of the contract, and they are requesting a 20% usage discount tied to committed capacity and a reduction to the standard service-credit cap (they want unlimited credits until remediation). They attached their forecast and the redlined SLA.

My read: customer is price-sensitive and volume is big enough that a small, time-boxed concession could lock their commit. Recommend we offer:
- Temporary uptime floor: 99.5% for a 6-month pilot window (auto-revert to 99.95% thereafter)
- Service-credit cap: 15% monthly cap (instead of unlimited)
- Discount: 15% off list pricing for 12-month commit (not 20%); we model margin impact below
- Operational mitigations: scheduled weekly maintenance windows during low traffic, priority routing on dedicated pool, and a shared runbook / 24-7 escalation path.

Attachments: Greenline_Demand_Forecast.xlsx (demand profile), Redline_SLA_v3.pdf (their redlines).

Need exec signoff on the SLA concession + pricing trade (or guidance if finance needs to counter). If ok, I can loop in legal for final redline and run DocuSign.

Thanks,

—Marissa

Subject: RE: Fwd: Greenline AI — SLA/discount ask + proposed mitigation (econ review)

Team,

Thanks for the context. I ran a quick sensitivity on the 15% discount + 15% monthly service-credit cap. Key points:
- With Greenline's forecasted commit, a 15% list discount reduces gross margin by ~7 percentage points in Y1 but becomes accretive in Y2 assuming retention.
- A 15% monthly credit cap limits downside but leaves us exposed if they experience repeated partial outages; recommend a hard annual cap equal to 2x monthly cap (i.e., annual cap = 30% of one month's bill) to bound exposure.
- Preferable commercial structure: 12-month minimum term + commit volume (prepay/committed credits) in exchange for the discount.

I've attached Deal_Econ_Modeling_v2.csv with scenarios.

Questions for Sales: Can we replace the flat 15% discount with a tiered commit discount (10% base; 15% if commit >= projected forecast)? If not, we need explicit signoff to proceed with the 15% concession and the hard annual credit cap. Also confirm that the ops addendum (maintenance windows + priority routing) will be accepted by Greenline and that legal is comfortable with the auto-revert clause.

If we get signoff today, I will prepare the finance approval memo and mark the deal with the commercial exceptions.

-David
David Kim
Director, Revenue Operations & Finance
Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.com

All — confirming alignment and approval to proceed with the negotiated terms below (per Jon/Marissa discussion and David's econ constraints). I will document in HubSpot and route to legal for final redline + DocuSign.

Agreed commercial concessions (final):
- Uptime floor: 99.5% for a 6-month pilot window starting at contract go-live. Auto-revert to 99.95% at month 7.
- Service-credit cap: 15% monthly cap, with an annual hard cap equal to 30% of one month's bill (to limit extreme exposure).
- Discount: 15% off list pricing conditional on a 12-month minimum commitment and meeting the forecasted commit tier.
- Operational addendum: weekly low-impact maintenance windows (customer-approved schedule), priority routing to dedicated pool, and a 90-day telemetries/health-check cadence with shared runbook.
- Legal to include fallback clause: if commit tier falls below 70% of forecast in any month during the first 6 months, discount re-prices retroactively to 10% for the remaining term.

Jonas — please confirm this is within your approval threshold. David — please confirm finance memo will go out with these numeric caps so we can close. Marissa — once legal returns redline I will coordinate signature.

Thanks,
